Your phone never talks to GPS satellites. It only listens. 🛰️

About 30 satellites, more than 12,000 miles up, each with an atomic clock. Your phone times their signals and turns each delay into a distance. Four distances, one spot: you, accurate to about 16 feet.

There's a tiny weight inside your phone that never sits still. 📱

A 2 mm chip holds a sliver of silicon on microscopic springs. Tilt your phone, gravity pulls it, the gaps between its comb-like fingers change, and the chip reads that change hundreds of times a second. That's how your screen knows when to rotate, and how your phone counts your steps.

Your phone screen can't feel your finger. It feels the electricity in your body. ⚡

Under the glass is a grid of invisible wires. Your finger pulls a little charge from the crossings underneath, and a chip checking up to 240 times a second finds the spot. That's also why your screen ignores you when you're wearing gloves.

Your credit card has no battery. So how does it pay with just a tap? 💳

A thin coil inside the card picks up the reader's magnetic field, which powers its chip for a split second, just long enough to create a code that only works once. Your phone goes one step further: it never sends your real card number.

Your phone charger switches the power on and off over 100,000 times a second. 🔌

It turns your outlet's 120-volt back-and-forth current into one direction, chops it into rapid pulses, and a tiny transformer steps it down for your battery. Faster switching means a smaller transformer, which is why gallium nitride (GaN) chargers are so small. The warmth you feel? Up to about a tenth of the energy, lost as heat.
